newsitem.title: UK: UK press largely indifferent to EU summit deal.
newsitem.headline: UK press largely indifferent to EU summit deal.

text.p: British newspapers on Tuesday greeted the resolution of the EU row between France and Germany with the lukewarm indifference of a bystander on the issue of European monetary union(EMU).

With Britain already highly unlikely to take part in the first wave of a single currency planned for 1999, newspapers paid more attention to the election of a new Conservative Party leader and renewed violence in Northern Ireland than events in Amsterdam.
The influential Financial Times said the German government had never been likely to accept changes to the EMU stability pact negotiated a year ago.

"All France could hope for was the odd leaf or two. One is the new largely empty employment chapter....A little thing like the French elections was never likely to shift the euro-train off its tracks," the newspaper said in an editorial.
The Daily Telegraph said France had little choice but to capitulate.

"It seems as though nothing can stop Chancellor Kohl from securing monetary union on his own terms...All that the French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has won is a banal statement to the effect that the EU recognises the importance of jobs," it said in an editorial.
However the paper said there had been a change of attitude in Germany. "Ministers are increasingly listening to their exporters, who do not want a euro with a high exchange rate," it said.
